title: An isolated point of a fibre of a locally finite type morphism has finite residue field extension
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $x\in X$, put $s=f(x)$, and let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the fibre of $f$ at $s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. If the point of $X_s$ corresponding to $x$ is isolated in $X_s$ (the singleton is open in $X_s$), then the field extension $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)$ induced by $f$ on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] is finite, i.e. $\kappa(x)$ is a finite-dimensional $\kappa(s)$-vector space [def-pc-field-extension].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01TH (morphisms-lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize, line 3664), (2) => (1), and Lemma 01TG (morphisms-lemma-residue-field-quasi-finite, line 3652); used in this form in the proof of More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LM (more-morphisms.tex lines 12056-12059)

proof.text: Let $\sigma:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ be the canonical morphism, with image $s$, and $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ the fibre with projections $p:X_s\to X$ and $\pi:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]; $\pi$ is the base change of $f$ along $\sigma$. Since $f$ is locally of finite type, $\pi$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change] (with $g=\sigma$) [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] $p$ is a homeomorphism of $X_s$ onto the subspace $f^{-1}(s)\ni x$, so there is exactly one $\xi\in X_s$ with $p(\xi)=x$; this is the point of $X_s$ corresponding to $x$, and by hypothesis $\{\xi\}$ is open in $X_s$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), proof of (2) => (1): 'X_s is ... locally of finite type over kappa(s)' (Lemma 01T4 lemma-base-change-finite-type)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-over-field-isolated-point-residue-finite] to the field $k=\kappa(s)$, the scheme $Y=X_s$, the morphism $g=\pi$ (locally of finite type by step 1) and the point $y=\xi$ (isolated by step 1): the homomorphism $\pi^\sharp:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(\xi)$ induced by $\pi$ on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] makes $\kappa(\xi)$ a finite extension of $\kappa(s)$. Here the residue field of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ at its unique point $\eta$ is identified with $\kappa(s)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] (with $R=\kappa(s)$, $\mathfrak p=0$, where $\kappa(s)_{(0)}/0=\kappa(s)$); under this identification the map $\sigma^\sharp:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(\eta)$ induced by $\sigma$ is the identity, because $\sigma$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the residue map $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\kappa(s)$ followed by $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}\to S$, so on stalks at $\eta$ it is $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\kappa(s)$ itself, which induces the identity of $\kappa(s)$ on residue fields.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00PJ (lemma-isolated-point), (1) => (6), through Morphisms, Lemma 01TH (2) => (4) and Lemma 01TG, which deduce finiteness of the residue field extension from the isolatedness of x in an affine open of the fibre

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field] to $f:X\to S$, $g=\sigma:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ and $z=\xi$, so that $p(\xi)=x$, $\pi(\xi)=\eta$ and $f(x)=s=\sigma(\eta)$ (residue fields and induced maps as in [def-weil-residue-field]). With $\kappa(\eta)=\kappa(s)$ and $\sigma^\sharp=\mathrm{id}$ (step 2), the ring $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(\eta)$ is $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(s)$, which is isomorphic to the field $\kappa(x)$ by $a\otimes b\mapsto a\,f^\sharp(b)$ (here $f^\sharp:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)$ is induced by $f$). A field has only the prime ideal $0$, so the prime $\mathfrak p$ attached to $\xi$ is $0$ and the quotient by it is the field $\kappa(x)$. The lemma gives that the induced map $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(s)\to\kappa(\xi)$, $a\otimes b\mapsto p^\sharp(a)\pi^\sharp(b)$, is an isomorphism of fields, compatible with the maps from $\kappa(x)$ and from $\kappa(s)$. Composing with the isomorphism $\kappa(x)\cong\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(s)$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, the map $p^\sharp:\kappa(x)\to\kappa(\xi)$ is an isomorphism; and since $1\otimes b=f^\sharp(b)\otimes1$ in the tensor product, $\pi^\sharp(b)=p^\sharp(f^\sharp(b))$ for $b\in\kappa(s)$, i.e. $p^\sharp$ is an isomorphism of extensions of $\kappa(s)$ (with $\kappa(s)$ acting on $\kappa(x)$ by $f^\sharp$ and on $\kappa(\xi)$ by $\pi^\sharp$).

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01TF (lemma-closed-point-fibre-locally-finite-type), proof: 'kappa(x) = kappa(q) = kappa(q-bar)'; the residue field of a point of a fibre product, Schemes, Lemma 01JT (schemes-lemma-points-fibre-product)

proof.text: By step 3, $p^\sharp$ is a $\kappa(s)$-linear bijection $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(\xi)$, so $\dim_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(x)=\dim_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(\xi)$, which is finite by step 2. Hence $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)$ (the map induced by $f$) is a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension].
